cards.front: Which two coverages are needed before registering, and what does each pay?
cards.back: Registration needs injury and property coverage first, with injury benefits paying your own hurt regardless of fault and property benefits paying damage you cause others.
cards.memory_hook: Injury pays you, property pays others

cards.front: What minimum coverage must owners carry, and where is proof kept?
cards.back: Owners prove coverage at registration, carry at least ten thousand dollars of each kind from a Florida-licensed carrier, keep it continuous, and keep proof in the car.

cards.front: Which cars must stay insured, and what happens on a lapse?
cards.back: Cars present ninety days in the last three hundred sixty-five must stay insured, carriers report lapses to the state, failures suspend for up to three years, and plates go back before policies cancel.

cards.front: What happens to a stopped driver who has no proof of insurance?
cards.back: Stopped drivers without proof must prove coverage in court or face suspension, and convicted lapses reinstate between one hundred fifty dollars and five hundred dollars.
cards.memory_hook: No proof? Prove it in court

cards.front: What penalties follow an insurance suspension lasting more than a month?
cards.back: Suspensions past thirty days allow plate seizure and jail time up to a year with a one thousand dollars fine, bar temporary licenses, punish fake cards as misdemeanors, and grant hearings on request.
cards.memory_hook: Long lapse risks plates and jail

cards.front: How do crash drivers and DUI convicts prove financial responsibility?
cards.back: Crash drivers prove financial responsibility by insurance or state certificate, and DUI convicts carry one hundred thousand dollars, three hundred thousand dollars, and fifty thousand dollars tiers for three years.

cards.front: What coverage tiers apply to point, crash and serious-offense cases?
cards.back: Point, crash, habitual-offender, and serious-offense cases carry ten thousand dollars, twenty thousand dollars, and ten thousand dollars tiers or thirty thousand dollars combined, with lapses suspending up to three years and at-fault damages prepaid.

cards.front: How does injury coverage differ from property coverage?
cards.back: Injury coverage pays your own hurt no matter the fault while property coverage pays damage you inflict on others.

cards.front: What are the coverage minimums, and how is a lapse suspension avoided?
cards.back: Minimums sit at ten thousand dollars each from a licensed carrier, and lapses suspend up to three years unless plates surrender first.

cards.front: How does missing proof differ from a forged insurance card?
cards.back: Missing proof forces a court date while a forged card forces an arrest, and month-old suspensions allow plate seizure.
cards.memory_hook: Missing means court, forged means arrest

cards.front: How do the DUI responsibility tiers compare with the lesser tiers?
cards.back: DUI tiers run one hundred thousand dollars, three hundred thousand dollars, and fifty thousand dollars for three years against ten thousand dollars, twenty thousand dollars, and ten thousand dollars or thirty thousand dollars combined for lesser triggers.

decks.module: Teen curfews, license crimes, disabled parking

cards.front: When may learner minors and sixteen- and seventeen-year-olds drive?
cards.back: Learner minors drive daylight only until three months pass, then to ten pm, while sixteen-year-olds stop from eleven pm to six am and seventeen-year-olds from one am to five am, all excused for work or a twenty-one-plus companion.

cards.front: Which acts count as license crimes?
cards.back: License crimes span altering, misusing, lending, fraudulent applications, dual credentials, unlicensed loans and rentals, and false statements to officers, courts, or crash reports.

cards.front: What do disabled permits allow, and what happens when one is borrowed?
cards.back: Disabled permits waive meter fees and open reserved spaces while transporting the owner, and borrowed permits draw misdemeanor charges, five hundred dollars or six months, plus towing and confiscation.

cards.front: How do the curfews for sixteen- and seventeen-year-olds differ?
cards.back: Sixteen-year-olds stop from eleven pm to six am while seventeen-year-olds stop from one am to five am, both excused for work or a senior companion.
cards.memory_hook: Eleven to six, one to five

cards.front: How does a borrowed disabled permit differ from a proper one?
cards.back: Borrowed disabled permits draw five hundred dollars or six months with towing, while proper permits waive meters and open reserved bays.

cards.front: What does DUI cover, and what happens at arrest?
cards.back: DUI covers driving or controlling a car under alcohol, controlled, prescription, or store-bought drugs, suspends at arrest for BAL point zero eight or refusal, and compels blood, urine, or breath tests by implied consent.

cards.front: What does refusing a chemical test cost?
cards.back: Test refusal suspends one year automatically, a second refusal stretches eighteen months with a misdemeanor, and fatal or injurious crashes force a professional blood draw even unconscious.

cards.front: What are the penalties for a first DUI?
cards.back: A first DUI draws five hundred dollars to one thousand dollars, fifty service hours, a year of probation, six months jailed, one hundred eighty revoked days, twelve school hours, an addiction check, and possible interlock, all harsher with high BAL or a young rider.

cards.front: What are the penalties for a second DUI?
cards.back: A second DUI draws one thousand dollars to two thousand dollars, nine months jailed, one hundred eighty revoked days, twenty-one school hours, an addiction check, and a year of interlock, doubled in fines when enhanced.

cards.front: What are the penalties for a third DUI?
cards.back: A third DUI draws two thousand dollars to five thousand dollars, twelve months jailed, one hundred eighty revoked days, twenty-one school hours, an addiction check, and two interlock years.

cards.front: What alcohol rules apply to drivers under twenty-one?
cards.back: Under-twenty-one drivers lose six months at BAL point zero two, take a substance course at point zero five, trigger parent notice under nineteen, and lose the license for any drug conviction.

cards.front: What can happen to a car used in a drug felony?
cards.back: Cars hauling, selling, or abetting drug felonies may be seized and forfeited as contraband.

cards.front: What does DUI include, and how are tests compelled?
cards.back: DUI spans alcohol through store-bought drugs, suspends at arrest for BAL point zero eight or refusal, and compels tests by signed consent.

cards.front: How does a first refusal compare with a second?
cards.back: A first refusal costs one year while a second costs eighteen months plus a misdemeanor, and bloody crashes force draws regardless.

cards.front: How do DUI penalties change from first to third conviction?
cards.back: DUI fines, jail, schooling, and interlock all climb across first, second, and third convictions with high-BAL enhancement.

cards.front: What happens to under-twenty-one drivers at low alcohol levels?
cards.back: Under-twenty-one drivers fall at BAL point zero two for six months, study at point zero five, and trigger parent notice under nineteen.
cards.memory_hook: Point zero two costs six months

cards.front: What are the penalties for roadway litter?
cards.back: Roadway litter up to fifteen pounds costs one hundred dollars, while heavier dumps bring misdemeanor charges, one thousand dollars, three points, and cleanup duty.

cards.front: What does illegally passing a school bus cost?
cards.back: Bus passing draws a citation, school, four points, and two hundred sixty-five dollars or four hundred sixty-five dollars, while injurious passing adds one hundred twenty service hours, a panel, six points, a year out, and one thousand five hundred dollars.

cards.front: How must belts be worn, and where do young children ride?
cards.back: Rim driving damages roads unlawfully, belts must cross hips and chest rather than hiding behind backs since airbags never substitute, and child seats must fit child, car, and caregiver with under-thirteen riders behind.
cards.memory_hook: Hips and chest, kids in back

cards.front: Who must be belted, and which children need car seats?
cards.back: Rear-facing seats never face airbags, hired-ride restraints fall on parents, belts bind drivers, front riders, and under-eighteen passengers, under-four riders need seats with four-and-five riders seated or boosted, drivers answer for minors while adults answer for themselves, and fitting help runs free.

cards.front: Who is exempt from seat belt rules?
cards.back: Belt exemptions cover certified medical cases, paper carriers, old school buses, paid buses, farm gear, trucks past twenty-six thousand pounds, and favor or emergency rides for ages four and five.

cards.front: How do penalties for light and heavy litter differ?
cards.back: Litter to fifteen pounds costs one hundred dollars while heavier loads bring a misdemeanor, one thousand dollars, three points, and cleanup.

cards.front: How does plain bus passing differ from injurious bus passing?
cards.back: Plain bus passing costs points and hundreds while injurious passing costs service hours, a year out, and one thousand five hundred dollars.

cards.front: How must belts fit, and where do children under thirteen ride?
cards.back: Belts cross hips and chest with airbags never substituting, and under-thirteen riders belong behind.

cards.front: Which ages need car seats, and who answers for each rider?
cards.back: Under-four riders need seats with ages four and five seated or boosted, drivers answer for minors, and adults answer for themselves.

cards.front: Which groups are exempt from belt rules?
cards.back: Belt exemptions favor medical cases, paper routes, old buses, paid buses, farm gear, and heavy trucks past twenty-six thousand pounds.

cards.front: What is Florida's maximum speed limit, and what does speeding cost?
cards.back: Every motorist must know and obey limits, Florida caps them at seventy miles per hour, and speeding tickets cost fines and points.

cards.front: What fines apply to extreme speeding and zone speeding?
cards.back: Exceeding limits past fifty miles per hour costs one thousand dollars then two thousand five hundred dollars, and school or work-zone speeding doubles fines toward one thousand dollars with a possible course.

cards.front: When must a crash driver take a collision-avoidance course?
cards.back: Charged crash drivers face court on officer-filed counts, and at-fault injury crashes or second collisions in two years force a collision-avoidance course.

cards.front: What follows a third crash offense within three years?
cards.back: A third crash offense inside thirty-six months forces a twelve-hour advanced course, four wheel hours, and an extended test, lapsing to cancellation past ninety days.

cards.front: Which point totals suspend a license, and for how long?
cards.back: Point totals suspend thirty days at twelve in a year, three months at eighteen in eighteen months, and a year at twenty-four in thirty-six months, counting out-of-state convictions equally.

cards.front: What happens to a minor who reaches six points in a year?
cards.back: Minors reaching six points in a year drop to business-only driving for a year, extended ninety days per further point.

cards.front: How many points do speeding, leaving a scene and texting carry?
cards.back: Speeding draws three points to fifteen over, four past sixteen, and six in a crash, scene-leaving over fifty dollars draws six, and texting draws three plus three in school zones or six in a crash.

cards.front: How many points do signal, bus, reckless and curfew violations carry?
cards.back: Signals, bus passing, and reckless driving each draw four points, injurious bus passing draws six, and restricted-hour driving plus handheld use in protected zones draw three.

cards.front: How do extreme speeding fines compare with zone speeding fines?
cards.back: Speeding past fifty over costs one thousand dollars then two thousand five hundred dollars while zone speeding doubles toward one thousand dollars with a possible course.

cards.front: What must a driver with a third crash offense complete, and how soon?
cards.back: A third crash offense inside thirty-six months forces schooling, wheel hours, and an extended test within ninety days.

cards.front: Which point totals suspend adults, and when do minors drop to business-only?
cards.back: Point clocks suspend at twelve, eighteen, and twenty-four across lengthening windows, while minors fall to business-only at six.

cards.front: How do speeding and texting points step up?
cards.back: Speed points step three, four, six by margin and crash, and texting adds three alone, three in zones, or six in crashes.

cards.front: Which violations cost four, six or three points?
cards.back: Signals, bus passing, and recklessness cost four each, injurious bus passing costs six, and hour and handheld breaches cost three.

cards.front: Which grounds start a license suspension?
cards.back: Suspension starts with fraudulent applications, unlawful license use, court orders, and intoxication-test refusals.

cards.front: What other grounds continue a suspension?
cards.back: Suspension continues through restricted-license misuse, point totals, unpaid fines and no-shows, support lapses, missing insurance, bus failures, retail theft, and dropouts.

cards.front: Which grounds lead to revocation?
cards.back: Revocation ends privileges for intoxicated driving, vehicle felonies, deadly hit-and-runs, ownership lies, triple recklessness, vehicle immorality, major or point-count histories, drug felonies, failed vision, and racing.

cards.front: When is a license cancelled?
cards.back: Cancellation voids licenses issued wrongly, won by false papers, or tied to unfinished schooling.

cards.front: Where are hardship and reinstatement handled, and how fast must DUI appeals move?
cards.back: Hardship and reinstatement run through review offices, DUI alcohol and refusal appeals need hearings inside ten days of arrest, and first offenders may trade review rights for a restricted license there.

cards.front: How do suspension, revocation and cancellation differ?
cards.back: Suspension pauses privileges, revocation ends them, and cancellation voids them from the start.

cards.front: How soon must DUI alcohol and refusal appeals be heard?
cards.back: DUI alcohol and refusal appeals need review-office hearings inside ten days of arrest.

recap_hooks.text: Injury coverage pays your own injuries and property coverage pays damage you cause, with ten thousand dollars of each kept continuously.
Lapses can suspend a license, so plates go back before a policy is cancelled.

recaps.module: Teen curfews, license crimes, disabled parking

recap_hooks.text: Teen drivers have set curfews, and lending, altering or misusing a license is a crime.
Drivers have consented to testing, refusal costs a year, and DUI penalties climb with each conviction.
Drivers under twenty-one face strict low alcohol limits.
Passing a stopped school bus brings points and fines, and causing injury makes it far worse.
Belts cross hips and chest, young children ride in back, and drivers answer for minors.
Florida's top limit is seventy, and points add up to suspensions at twelve, eighteen and twenty-four.
Minors who reach six points in a year drop to business-only driving.
Suspension pauses a license, revocation ends it, and cancellation voids it from the start.
DUI alcohol and refusal appeals need a hearing request within ten days of arrest.
